name: Apigenin
description: Apigenin (CAS 520-36-5 ), also known commercially as Apigenol, is a naturally derived flavonoid extracted primarily from chamomile, parsley, and celery. It functions as a bioactive antioxidant ingredient across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic formulations. In dietary supplement manufacturing, this compound is incorporated into capsules, tablets, and functional beverages targeting antioxidant and wellness positioning. Cosmetic formulators use it as an active ingredient in anti-aging and skin-brightening topicals. Its antioxidant capacity supports product claims around oxidative stress protection in high-end skincare lines. Food and beverage producers source it as a natural colorant and functional additive, particularly in products where clean-label botanical ingredients are advantageous. Pharmaceutical researchers and contract manufacturers also use it as a reference standard or active botanical extract in preclinical and formulation development programs. This versatility makes it a staple for R&D departments across multiple industries. The product is supplied as a fine yellow powder, typically derived from chamomile flower extract or synthesized for higher purity applications. Standard market grades include 98%+ purity (HPLC) for pharmaceutical and research use. Lower-purity botanical extract forms are available for nutraceutical and cosmetic applications where full-spectrum profiles are preferred. Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D procurement to bulk quantities suited for commercial-scale formulation.
